 DATA ANALYTICS USING PYTHON – PRACTICAL EXAMINATION Duration: 2 Hours Maximum Marks: 100 Instructions: ● Write efficient and readable Python code. ● Use functions wherever appropriate. ● Use object-oriented programming wherever required. ● Avoid using built-in shortcuts unless explicitly permitted. ● Write comments wherever necessary. SECTION A – Python Programming (60 Marks) Question 1 (10 Marks) Create a Python program to manage employee information using classes. Your program should allow users to store employee details, calculate the annual salary, and identify employees whose annual salary exceeds ₹8,00,000. Question 2 (10 Marks) Given a list of student records stored as tuples containing student names and marks, write a Python program to: ● Find the highest-scoring student. ● Calculate the average marks. ● Display all students scoring above the average. ● Store the topper's details in a dictionary. 

[Page 2]
 Question 3 (10 Marks) A retail store maintains product-wise monthly sales data using a dictionary where each key represents a product and the corresponding value is a list of monthly sales.

3 (10 Marks) A retail store maintains product-wise monthly sales data using a dictionary where each key represents a product and the corresponding value is a list of monthly sales. Write a program to: ● Calculate the total sales of each product. ● Determine the highest-selling product. ● Compute the average sales of every product. ● Store the final summary in another dictionary. Question 4 (10 Marks) Given a paragraph of text, write a Python program without using the collections module to: ● Count the total number of words. ● Identify all unique words. ● Calculate the frequency of every word. ● Display the three most frequently occurring words. Question 5 (10 Marks) Write a menu-driven Python application for a list of integers that provides the following operations: ● Remove duplicate elements. ● Display all prime numbers. ● Display all even numbers. ● Display all odd numbers. ● Find the largest and smallest elements. ● Exit the application. Implement each operation using separate functions. Question 6 (10 Marks) Design a Bank Account Management System using classes.

The program should support: ● Depositing money. ● Withdrawing money. ● Checking the available balance. ● Maintaining a transaction history. ● Preventing invalid withdrawal and deposit operations. SECTION B – Exploratory Data Analysis (40 Marks) Use the dataset provided by the examiner. Question 7 (15 Marks) Load the dataset using Pandas and perform the following exploratory tasks: ● Display the first five records. ● Display the last five records. ● Display the shape of the dataset. ● Display the data types of all columns. ● Identify missing values. ● Identify duplicate records. ● Remove duplicate records if present. Question 8 (15 Marks) Perform descriptive statistical analysis on the dataset. Your program should compute: ● Mean ● Median ● Mode ● Standard Deviation ● Correlation Matrix 

[Page 4]
Based on your analysis, answer the following: ● Which feature has the strongest positive correlation with the target variable?

● Median ● Mode ● Standard Deviation ● Correlation Matrix 

[Page 4]
Based on your analysis, answer the following: ● Which feature has the strongest positive correlation with the target variable? ● Which feature has the weakest correlation with the target variable? ● Which numerical feature exhibits the highest variance? Question 9 (10 Marks) Using appropriate visualization libraries, generate the following plots: ● Histogram ● Box Plot ● Scatter Plot ● Correlation Heatmap Based on the generated visualizations, answer the following: ● Identify any outliers present in the dataset. ● Comment on the distribution of the numerical features. ● Identify any pair of highly correlated features. ● State which visualization is most suitable for detecting outliers and justify your answer. BONUS QUESTION (10 Marks) An e-commerce company stores customer order details as a list of dictionaries. Write a Python program to generate a customer-wise summary containing: ● Total number of orders placed. ● Total purchase amount. ● Average purchase amount. ● Customer with the highest expenditure. Your solution should make effective use of dictionaries, loops, functions, and classes wherever appropriate.
